statement: Separate the immutable replication TARGET from mutable replica IDENTITIES: desired replication factor is the declared partitions-row replica_count (schema default 3), never the length of the initial replica-id list, and getInitialReplicaIds hands back a copy so replica-identity churn cannot mutate the declaration. A minted replace-replica-<hex> is a new identity, not evidence that RF changed from 3 to 4.

constraints.statement: If this Quest changes source code, spawn a subagent verifier before audit and git handoff, then record a Solver finding with evidence subagent:<id>.

Desired replication factor is the declared partitions-row replica_count, falling back to the schema-declared default READ from PARTITIONS_SCHEMA rather than restated as a literal. It is never derived from how many replica identities exist. A minted replace-replica-<hex> is a new identity and must not move the target.

getInitialReplicaIds returns a COPY. The declaration was previously handed out by reference and pushed into by replica wiring, so one caller mutated the shared declaration for every later reader; a caller mutating its copy must not change what the next reader sees.

A partition with no partitions row has no declared policy and resolves as undeclared with factor 0, never borrowing the schema default. Borrowing it would invent a requirement the partition was never given and would erase the fail-closed unreadable-requirement case landed in S1. An array is not a policy row.

This supersedes the landed S1 receipt required-count-derives-from-initial-replica-ids, which became a false claim the moment the source changed. It is renamed to required-count-derives-from-declared-policy and rewritten to assert that identity churn cannot move the factor and that a partition declaring five is not satisfied by three distinct nodes.
The authority is a frozen projection carrying exactly replicationFactor and source; it mints no holders, no replica identities, no convergence and no readiness.
Proof is a deterministic node:test witness, every guard mutation-verified with a harness that asserts the patch anchor is unique, and no cloud run is part of the proof.
